skill.name: system-integration-validator
skill.description: Validates system integration before deployment. Use when checking ports, database connections, frontend-backend APIs, or debugging blocked/stuck workflows. Detects dead ends, bottlenecks, circular dependencies.
skill.summary: Checks ports, local databases, API contracts, and data flows before deployment.
skill.author: BarisSozen

security_audit.summary: All eight static findings are false positives caused by documented examples, Markdown code fences, and safe local diagnostics. The skill contains no automatic execution, credential handling, external destinations, or prompt injection instructions.

static_findings.snippet: lsof -i :$port > /dev/null 2>&1 && echo "⚠️ $port IN USE" || echo "✅ $port free"

finding_verdicts.reason: Lines 46-50 are a fenced Bash example using a fixed port list and local lsof checks. The Markdown fence is not Ruby backtick execution, and no untrusted command input is accepted.
Line 50 only closes the Markdown code fence for the port-check example. It does not execute a shell or Ruby command.
Lines 53-56 document local PostgreSQL and Redis readiness commands with fixed arguments. The Markdown fence is not backtick execution, and the example contains no attacker-controlled interpolation.
Line 56 only closes the fenced database-check example. It contains no executable backtick expression or dynamic command construction.
Line 67 opens a TypeScript example about fetch timeouts. It is a Markdown fence, not shell or Ruby execution.
The fetch call is explicitly labeled as a timeout anti-pattern in a documentation example. It names no external destination, sends no data, and is not automatically executed.
The fetch call demonstrates AbortController timeout handling in TypeScript documentation. It names no destination, transmits no credentials, and is not an operational network action.
The command redirects routine lsof output to the standard /dev/null sink. It does not read sensitive files, persist data, or modify the filesystem.

content.value_statement: Integration failures can block deployments through port conflicts, unavailable databases, or mismatched APIs. This skill provides a focused checklist for finding those problems early.
actual_capabilities: Provides a pre-deployment checklist for ports, databases, API contracts, and data flows.
Supplies a local port-check example for five common service ports.
Supplies PostgreSQL and Redis readiness command examples.
Guides comparison of frontend requests with backend API routes.
Identifies dead ends, orphan inputs, bottlenecks, circular dependencies, and missing request timeouts.
limitations: Provides guidance and examples, but includes no automated validation script.
The port example checks only five predefined local ports.
The database examples assume local PostgreSQL and Redis services with default ports.
API contract and data flow analysis require project files and architecture context.

use_cases.title: Check a Release Candidate
use_cases.description: Review service ports, database readiness, and integration blockers before a release reaches production.

use_cases.title: Trace an API Mismatch
use_cases.description: Compare frontend requests with backend routes to find missing endpoints, incompatible contracts, or unconsumed outputs.

use_cases.title: Diagnose a Blocked Workflow
use_cases.description: Map producers, consumers, and dependencies to identify dead ends, bottlenecks, or circular relationships.

prompt_templates.title: Check Local Ports
prompt_templates.prompt: Check local ports [ports] for conflicts and summarize each result before I deploy [service].
prompt_templates.scenario: Begin with a focused port availability check.

prompt_templates.title: Validate Database Readiness
prompt_templates.prompt: Validate PostgreSQL at [host and port] and Redis at [host and port]. Report connection failures and likely causes.
prompt_templates.scenario: Confirm required data services are reachable.

prompt_templates.title: Compare API Contracts
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare frontend endpoints in [frontend path] with backend routes in [backend path]. Report mismatches, missing consumers, and missing producers.
prompt_templates.scenario: Investigate integration errors between application layers.

prompt_templates.title: Audit the Complete Integration
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit [system] before deployment. Check ports, databases, API contracts, dead ends, bottlenecks, circular dependencies, and request timeouts. Rank blockers by impact.
prompt_templates.scenario: Perform an advanced review across the complete deployment path.

output_examples.input: Check ports 3000, 3001, and 5432 before deploying the web application.
output: Port 3001: in use; identify the owning process before deployment.
Port 5432: in use; confirm the PostgreSQL service owns the listener.
Deployment status: blocked until the port 3001 conflict is resolved.

output_examples.input: Review the checkout flow from the frontend through the payment API and database.
output: API contract: the frontend sends currency, but the backend route does not define it.
Data flow: the payment result has no consumer after the retry branch.
Reliability: the payment request has no timeout.
Priority: fix the contract mismatch before deployment.

best_practices: Provide the expected services, ports, routes, and dependency map before validation.
Run checks in a controlled environment with the required local tools installed.
Resolve blocking findings first, then repeat the complete checklist before deployment.
anti_patterns: Do not treat an occupied database port as a conflict before identifying its owning process.
Do not infer API compatibility from endpoint names without comparing request and response contracts.
Do not approve external requests that lack explicit timeouts and failure handling.

faq.question: Does this skill deploy applications?
faq.answer: No. It provides checks and analysis guidance before deployment.

faq.question: Which databases does it cover?
faq.answer: The included examples cover PostgreSQL and Redis on local default ports.

faq.question: Can it find port conflicts?
faq.answer: Yes. It provides a local lsof example for ports 3000, 3001, 5432, 6379, and 8080.

faq.question: Does it automatically inspect API schemas?
faq.answer: No. You must provide frontend and backend files or contract details for comparison.

faq.question: What data flow problems can it identify?
faq.answer: It guides detection of dead ends, orphan inputs, high-input bottlenecks, and circular dependencies.

faq.question: Does it make external network requests?
faq.answer: No. The fetch calls are documentation examples that compare missing and configured request timeouts.
